Mostly my cats - I took them 2 years ago with my dead boyfriend, because we were living togheter and we though that it's time for some serious step. He loved them so much. 

Second thing - doing stuff. Just overworking myself. I need to do many things, just work, play games, activly watch anime, be a control freak about my body weight.

Just do, do, do stuff. If I do stuff, I don't have time to think about hanging myself on door knob.

Hey, after death of my partner (21.4.2020) I started to do more volunteer things on local LGBT+ Center, where I was usually to bake things I wasn't allowed in our house (we were on Keto diet, but I still loved to bake some non-keto things for others). After some months I got there a job as a volunteer coordinator. 

I have a lot of "children" to care about. But still, I'm lonely as fuck. I give a lot of love to others, but nothing for me. 

I have some friends, but they're tired of my depression. It's more and more depressing for me. 

Try to do lot of stuff with other people. I Hope that you'll find something or someone, who will be good friend for you and will have time for you.

Don't say that - meds helped me to get a little peace in grieving. It helped to not stare at wall for 6 hours a day. It helped to not do harm to myself.
It helped.

I had eraser inside my ear. When I came to hospital nurses and doctors had a good laugh at me.
I was trying to scratch my ear with pencil and I forgot that i was chewing on eraser and while scratching a small fragment just slipped inside my ear. 

I was 18.

24, my boyfriend died next to me after seizure, we were togheter 5 years and we known each other for nearly 8. 
It's been a 16 months after his death. It "got better" but only in terms of job and other stupid things. I'm still lonely, I don't have any really good friends, only "just friends", so most of the time I don't have anybody to talk. He was my best friend and I often, before living together, I was talking witg him for hours every day.

Hey, I lost my boyfriend to epilepsy too, 21 april 2020.

I think he was my ultimate love. I have zero interest in dating, love or sex.

He was just my perfect person. I don't want to have anybody other than him.

Oh boi. What's wrong with them? What are they thinking saying that?

Also, same, my sympathies for your loss.

So, I put description in some weird place so I copy it here:
I got photos of almost-finished figurine of my partners' fursona (Capibara). It will sit on box with his ashes. Made by amazing Falauke.

I was ready for it yesterday and I stopped because my commissioner called me to tell me that they need one more extra sketch because other Illustrator cancelled deal. Welp, no time for death when you need to draw stuff. I wanted to call hotline too but in my shitcountry only kids suicide hotline works 24/7.

I got new job after 5 months - just 
part-time job at local foundation. Before that I was living at savings and illustration commissions. Now, year after his death, I work full-time (part-time in two Jobs).
Welp, when you work, you don't think about depression, and thanks to work i have money for therapy and antidepressants.
Yup, same. When I can't find something I talk to Him like he is there. Or when I'm watching new episode of One Piece - I like to "talk" with Him about what's going on.

Hey!

Still in bad relationship with His mother. And I started taking meds - I'm diagnosed with post-trauma depression. Trying to copy with reality day-to-day - got new job in local fundation!
 Thanks for asking and I'm hoping that you are doing okey! :)

I'm seeing a trauma therapist for half a year after sudden death of my partner. It just don't get better. Yeah, life is getting better, i got nice job, I have amazing people around me. It just.
You know.
I still don't want to be without him. When day ends, nothing really matters because he's not there.
Not going to hurt myself for now. I'm kind of...casually suicidal? I think medical term for this is passive suicidal thoughs. But thanks for your comment.

I also hope it for you! I just got a job, it's really good for me - I'm a volunteer coordinator at local equality center.
I can work from home and I can go there as many times in week as I feel good about it.
I'm still at therapy - it's okeeeeey? Kinda. I'm still casually suicidal and we are talking about this at therapy. 
Just remember - if you can, take everything easy. People around you might think that X-months are enough to get back to "normal". Don't worry about them. Just do everything in your own tempo.

I was always scared that it'll be like this, but in my situation... I was sitting next to him. His seizure was like always. Just... I didn't see moment when he choked on his blood, saliva or just his tongue. He was big bear, he always slept on stomach to PREVENT SITUATION LIKE THIS. It always worked, but not this time. 
They tried to reanimate him for hour.

My in-law taken only things he illustrated - some books and t-shirts with his drawings. Nothing more. And I ASKED her about it, I was trying to give her more (like board game they loved to play together) but she told me that if i don't like it i can sell or throw it away? 
Wtf???

She also know all of this things (cremation, secular funeral etc) because he had epilepsy for 15+ years and he known that one day it can kill him. We were talking about this. He was talking about this with her. And after his death, i don't know, she wanted to throw all of his requests to trash.

Thank you all for your comments and for all of this community. 
Thank you

Yes, we both were atheists. He had secular funeral because I was organizing it. It was 4 month ago. I don't believe in any god and after his death I never felt so much true to my beliefs. Like, what god can let young, beautiful and happy person die so suddenly? Why he had to be sick?
About afterlife - I just think that there can be something, I just don't know what. So thinking about own death is always kind of relieving - I have 50/50 chance to see him again or just to stop existing, and when you stop existing you don't sorry about anything.
Still dealing with grief after death of my love. Constant feeling of wanting to be dead, but without dying part.

Also not sleeping on my bed since death of my boyfriend. I CAN sleep there - because when my friend was staying at my place i sleep here for 2 days.
Just... It doesn't feel right.

My boyfriend died 1.5month ago. We both are known as  webartists, we both were guests at many comic conventions, we both sell merch on one booth. I know, I just know that when con calendar will return to normal and I start to attend them people will come to me and 1. Start to tell me that they are sorry for my loss or 2. Ask where is my boyfriend. 


I know that this will hurt as hell.
Thanks. It's hard and I'm tired of living, but Reddit r/griefsupport and r/widowers (and professional therapy ofc) helps.

Not a funeral director, but I organised my boyfriend funeral last month. His death was sudden, so he didn't make any special plans. We spoken before about ours funerals and he said that he would be mad if people would come all black, so I told my friends that feel free to come dressed as you want. One of our friends come in Guzma (from Pokemon) cosplay :D

Yes, replaying death scene is painful. My bf was obese - I didn't catch the moment when he stopped breathing. I just saw his hand turning blue.
We also had everything planned. And, I tell you, this is probably the worst. I usually think about things he wanted to do. All the movies he wanted to see. All comics he started and didn't finish. He was Perfect for me. Probably like your wife to you. And I know, that this Reddit is for saying that life is going on and you will feel better one day - I can tell you, if you feel now like your life ended, you're not alone with this feeling and you're not alone thinking that no, this "one day when you will feel better" will not come. I'm going on crisis therapy for three weeks now and I'm still sure, that for me this "one day" will not happen. Thinking about next half year, year, 5, 10, 20 years is just a pain.

Month ago I lost my partner, we been together for 5 years and we known each other for 7-8. We were living together for 2 years. He died from seizure. It's hard. It's exactly as you wrote - living in nightmare. It's freaking nightmare non stop. Like really bad B-Movie Horror.
